prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth strip supports a coarse layered layout: the bed and nearby seated/reclining camera wearer’s body occupy the near foreground (roughly 0.2–0.8 m), while another person beside the bed is generally about 0.8–1.5 m away; walls, floor, and background furniture are farther, approximately 1.5–3 m. Across the five frames, the camera turns around the bed, moving the nearby person from the upper/right region toward the edge or out of view, while the wearer’s arms and legs remain closest and intermittently occlude the bed. Bright foreground regions make near limbs and surfaces easier to separate than in RGB and show which items are likely within the wearer’s arm’s reach, especially the bed, dark garment, and nearby person. The map is unreliable at image boundaries, dark voids, thin structures, and overlapping limbs, and its relative brightness does not support precise metre estimates or dependable distances between partially occluded people.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates several person instances from the bed and background, showing that people or body parts overlap the bed and one another even where their clothing and the bedding have similar RGB appearance. It places the nearest wearer-visible limbs across the lower or central foreground, another person mostly above or to the right of the bed at roughly 0.8–1.5 m, and labels large bed regions directly in front of the wearer and within arm’s reach; much of the remaining scene is unlabeled black. Over the five frames, labeled person regions shift laterally and become cropped or occluded as the viewpoint rotates, while the bed expands across the middle frames and then becomes less completely segmented. The map does not reliably indicate metric distance, gaze, or facing direction, and several masks are fragmented, mislabeled, merged with bedding, or missing, so apparent person counts and separations are uncertain.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates visible hand configurations: magenta hand skeletons occur near the left/lower area in frame 1, upper-left and center-right in frame 2, near the center-right in frame 3, near the center in frame 4, and toward the right in frame 5, revealing hand locations that are difficult to distinguish against patterned fabric in RGB. These hands appear roughly 0.3–1.2 m from the camera and close to the bed or dark garment, with some likely within the camera wearer’s reach, but no dependable full-body skeleton is visible. Their movement across the strip mainly reflects changing viewpoint and partial hand motion, with hands entering, leaving, or being cropped by the frame; the map cannot establish whether people face or look toward the wearer because heads, torsos, and gaze landmarks are absent. The detections are unreliable because several skeletons float without connected arms, some visible limbs receive no pose, finger geometry is noisy, and overlapping or partly occluded hands may be assigned incompletely.
